_doc: One profile per TI board that is a port target. hw: the peripherals and blocks the board has, in vocab.json tags. hw_from_sdk means the tag is backed by a SysConfig module in that board's own SDK examples (inventory.py computes the union; feasibility.py merges it in). hw_extra lists tags the SDK examples do not show but the board has, each with its public source. hw_missing lists tags the examples might suggest but the board does not have. layers: the software layers an example can land on, with how (native: the board's own SDK ships it; shim: a header in portability/shim/ maps the names; partial: some blocks share names, others do not; size: fits only on paper, check RAM). flash_kb and ram_kb from data/boards.csv. zephyr: upstream, fork, out-of-tree or none (docs/research/portability-approaches-2026-10-06.md, 2026-10-06 reading). bridges: for a (layer, from family, to family) the port mechanism and the evidence row in portability/matrix.csv.

mspm0c1104.name: LP-MSPM0C1104
mspm0c1104.notes: 1 KB of RAM is the wall: FreeRTOS and TI Drivers images do not fit (experiment 2026-10-08-mspm0c1104-1kb-ram). 20-pin package runs out of pins on ports (X4, X18). TI's own C1104 driver examples show no CAN or COMP module.

mspm0l1306.name: LP-MSPM0L1306
mspm0l1306.notes: TI Drivers libraries ship for L13xx but no example and no board config (X23). FreeRTOS does not fit 4 KB with TI's settings (X23).

mspm0g3507.name: LP-MSPM0G3507
mspm0g3507.notes: Borrowed; not answering the debugger since 2026-10-05. The G3519 stands in for it.

mspm0g3519.name: LP-MSPM0G3519
mspm0g3519.notes: Largest MSPM0 on the bench; the natural landing board for every MSPM0 example (X: G3507 to G3519 185 of 270 built, roadmap P8).

mspm0g5187.name: LP-MSPM0G5187

hw_extra.NPU: TI product page MSPM0G5187 (NPU); 12 edgeAI NPU examples in the SDK

mspm0g5187.notes: TI Drivers: the SDK ships the libraries; examples per board not checked (partial).

mspm33c321a.name: LP-MSPM33C321A
mspm33c321a.notes: No TI Drivers at all (X6). DriverLib shares every GPIO, UART and timer name with MSPM0; SPI, I2C and ADC are new blocks, UNICOMM and HSADC (X7). PKA, SHA, AESADV, TRNG on chip. Whether its ai examples use an NPU or the CPU is not confirmed here; NPU left out of hw until read from TI's page.

cc2340r5.name: LP-EM-CC2340R5

hw_extra.RADIO_THREAD: F3 SDK 9.21 ships thread examples for the CC2340R5 (experiment 2026-10-05-cc2340r5-thread-full-device)

cc2340r5.notes: The house Zigbee light runs on it: any silicon run backs up and restores (boards.json). CAN seen once in its SDK (a can example) but the chip has no CAN controller: the example drives an external one; treat CAN as missing.

cc2755p10.name: LP-EM-CC2755P10

hw_extra.RADIO_THREAD: F3 SDK thread examples; OpenThread FTD ran 2026-10-09
hw_extra.HSM: CC27xx HSM (TI product page); cc2755p10/recovery notes
hw_extra.DMA: CC27xx has a DMA (uDMA) per TI product page; no SysConfig module in the driver examples

cc2755p10.notes: Same F3 SDK as the CC2340R5: 33 of 33 driver examples build for both (X11).

cc1354p10.name: LP-CC1354P10-1

hw_extra.RADIO_RF: Sub-1 GHz and 2.4 GHz multi-band (TI product page)

cc1354p10.notes: Its SDK (F2, simplelink_cc13xx_cc26xx_sdk 8.33) is not installed on this Mac any more (1.8 GB), so its own examples are not in the inventory; the hw list is set by hand from the 253-of-261 build sweep in cc1354p10/sweep/examples.csv and X12 to X14. F2 has no I2CTarget driver (X14).

cc35x1.name: LP-EM-CC35X1

hw_extra.DMA: SimpleLink Wi-Fi SDK uses uDMA under the drivers; no SysConfig module in the examples
hw_extra.QSPI: external 8 MB flash IS25WJ064F on the board (inventory.md)

cc35x1.notes: Wi-Fi 6 plus BLE. Its SDK is the smallest tree here (32 examples per board), all TI Drivers and FreeRTOS. Matter runs over Wi-Fi, not Thread.

am13e230.name: LP-AM13E230

hw_extra.NPU: 12 TI AI examples ran on the NPU 2026-10-09 (roadmap)
hw_extra.TMU: AM13E230 TMU (SDK mathlib and TMU experiments)

am13e230.notes: Prototype silicon, short-term SDK 26.01.00.03. AM13 driverlib carries about 530 MSPM0-name redirect macros (X8), and the SDK ships an STM32G4 HAL compatibility layer (X9). No SysConfig module for timer PWM (X8).

am263p.name: LP-AM263P
am263p.zephyr: none (no AM263 in upstream boards, 2026-10-06 reading)
am263p.notes: Crypto is behind the HSM client, not AES or SHA driver modules. Flash is external OSPI (32 MB); RAM is the 3 MB on-chip figure from data/boards.csv. RADIO_THREAD seen once in its SDK is a networking example name, not a radio: treated as missing. Probe dropped off USB 2026-10-09 22:25.

f2800137.name: LAUNCHXL-F2800137

hw_extra.DAC: F280013x has no buffered DAC (TI data sheet: CMPSS DAC only); left missing

f2800137.notes: Different instruction set (C28x) and compiler (TI C2000 25.11): only Plain C moves without a rewrite; every Arm layer is Does not exist here. CAN: F280013x has one CAN (DCAN) per TI; the C2000Ware can examples build for it. Not plugged in right now (2026-10-10 21:30).

f28p65x.name: LAUNCHXL-F28P65X
f28p65x.notes: C2000Ware on this Mac has device_support and driverlib for f280013x only, so the F28P65x examples are not installed and not in the inventory; the hw list is by hand from the F28P65x data sheet summary (dual C28x, CLA, 16-bit ADCs, DACs, FSI, EtherCAT not counted). Not plugged in right now (2026-10-10 21:30).

tda4.name: SK-TDA4VM
tda4.zephyr: none for the A72 Linux path
tda4.notes: Linux processor board: TI's examples for it live in the Processor SDK on the board, not in any SDK on this Mac, so it is a target only, and only the Plain C layer reaches it (X33). Hardware list from the kit's documents, not from SDK examples.

iwrl6432.name: IWRL6432BOOST

hw_extra.RADAR: 60 GHz front end, IWRL6432 data sheet
hw_extra.RADAR_HWA: hardware accelerator for FFT and CFAR (SDK hwa driver examples)

iwrl6432.probe: RI32RI32 (XDS110 on the board; flashing goes through the SOP switches and arprog over the serial port)
iwrl6432.notes: MMWAVE-L-SDK 05.05.04.02 installed 2026-10-11 (Linux-only installer, run in an Ubuntu 22.04 x86_64 VM on a Mac, tree copied to ~/ti on this Mac without docs). The SDK is MCU+ derived: same /drivers/* and /kernel/dpl SysConfig modules and makefile layout as the AM263Px SDK, so AM263P driver examples are the cross-family candidates. Flash backup is not possible (no read-back tool, RD1); the restore image is TI's Motion and Presence 2D prebuilt from the Radar Toolbox, which the board carries now. Flashing needs S1 position 1 off then S2 (a hand on the board).

bridges._doc: Port mechanism per (layer, from family, to family). kind: same_sdk (retarget device and board in SysConfig, app untouched), shim (header in portability/shim, app untouched), partial (names shared for some blocks), rewrite (nothing shared), none (layer absent on the target). evidence: matrix.csv row or page.

MSPM0->MSPM33.evidence: X28 (drop-in: 20 of 82 built, 19 ran) and X29 (configuration port: 43 of 83 built, run on the board); DMA, I2C and SPI-with-DMA differ (UNICOMM, DMA0)

MSPM33->MSPM0.evidence: none; the reverse of X28 is not run

MSPM0->AM13.evidence: X8 (3 of 3 ran) and X31 (10 of 31 GPIO, UART, SysTick examples build, 8 of 8 ran clean, LEDs seen toggling)

MSPM33->AM13.evidence: none; inferred from X7 and X8

F3->F2.evidence: X12 (8 of 8 built; F2 lacks I2CTarget)

F3->WIFI.evidence: none yet; same /ti/drivers module names (UART2, GPIO, SPI, I2C, Display) in both SDKs (inventory)

AM263P->MMWAVE.evidence: none yet; same /drivers module ids and makefile layout (inventory 2026-10-11); cores differ (R5F to M4F), DMA is EDMA on both

MMWAVE->AM263P.evidence: none yet; radar and HWA examples Do not make sense on the AM263P

*.evidence: FreeRTOS is in every SDK here except C2000Ware core; the port files differ per core

size_rules._doc: An example fits on paper when its native text+data is under the target flash and data+bss under the target RAM, each with 10 percent headroom. Sizes come from this repo's sweeps (341 of 3,302 examples have one, 2026-10-10).
